- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–25% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts spikes in price (e.g., 6.47 → 11.79) — apply “overshoot correction”: cap forecast at 1.5x historical max in 7-day window if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows mean-reversion bias — if recent 7-day average is >1.70, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 10 days; if <1.50, increase by 5–10%.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) correlate with model overestimating; apply “sentiment lag” rule: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before forecast, reduce forecast by 20–30% to account for delayed reaction.
- Model underestimates low-volume periods (e.g., 0.46 → 0.28) — if sentiment is flat or negative, add 10–20% buffer to forecast for low-activity windows.
